case_name: Saraffian v. SMBD Jewish General Hospital
text:
COURT OF APPEAL

CANADA

PROVINCE OF QUEBEC

REGISTRY OF

MONTREAL

No:

500-09-014687-040

(500-17-013166-023)

DATE:

November 19, 2004

PRESENT
:

THE HONOURABLE

ALLAN R. HILTON, J.A.

HANNA
SARAFFIAN

APPELLANT – Defendant and
Cross-Plaintiff

Petitioner on the motion

v.

SMBD-JEWISH
GENERAL HOSPITAL

RESPONDENT
– Plaintiff and Cross-Defendant

Respondent
on the motion

JUDGMENT

[
1
]

As judge in chambers, I have before me a motion
of Hanna Saraffian to suspend that part of a judgment of the Superior Court
which she has appealed that declared her to be a vexatious litigant,
[1]

and which ordered provisional execution of that conclusion notwithstanding
appeal. As the case in this Court has already been the subject of several
motions and judgments, I believe it essential to set out the procedural
framework within which Ms. Saraffian's current motion falls.

[
2
]

The saga began with an action on account brought
by the SMBD – Jewish General Hospital (the Hospital) against
Ms. Saraffian's mother, Martha Kummerman, as well as Ms. Saraffian
both personally and in her capacity as the administrator of her mother's
property under the terms of a power of attorney executed in 1998. The action
sought the recovery of money allegedly owing as fees for long term care lodging
provided to Mrs. Kummerman, as well as an order for them to pay the cost
of any future lodging. Ms. Saraffian appeared on her own behalf and
purported as well to represent Mrs. Kummerman on the basis that she was
empowered to do so by reason of the terms of the power of attorney.

[
3
]

Ms. Saraffian thus responded with a
cross-demand in her own name in which she claimed $400,000 for harassment and
loss of income. She also asserted a cross-demand on behalf of her mother
claiming $590,000. On the first day of the trial, the judge struck the defence
and cross‑demand of Mrs. Kummerman on the basis that
Ms. Saraffian could not act on her behalf before the courts, with the
result that the case proceeded by default against Mrs. Kummerman.
Ms. Saraffian's contestation of the Hospital's claim and her cross‑demand,
however, proceeded as a contested case on the merits.

[
4
]

On the fourth day of the trial, after it had
been adjourned for a week, the Hospital served and presented a motion to have
Ms. Saraffian declared a vexatious litigant. Without going into all of the
details, the motion alleged a series of threats said to have been made by
Ms. Saraffian to continue suing the Hospital, whether in Quebec or
possibly even in the State of New York, where the power of attorney under which
she is acting for her mother had been executed. It also referred to a series of
other cases in which Ms. Saraffian had been involved either as a plaintiff
or a defendant, and asserted that Ms. Saraffian "continuously/repeatedly
submits the same type of allegations in all of these cases: fraud, injustice,
violation of her rights, loss of revenue due to psychological harassment,
etc.".

[
5
]

The lengthy judgment of the Superior Court,
which was rendered promptly after having been reserved, maintained the
Hospital's action against Mrs. Kummerman and Ms. Saraffian, but only
in the latter's representative and not personal capacity, for past and future
costs of lodging at the Hospital. It also dismissed Ms. Saraffian's cross
demand, and maintained the Hospital's motion to have her declared a vexatious
litigant. The operative part of the latter conclusions of the judgment read as
follows:

[95]      DECLARES that Defendant
Hanna Saraffian behaves in a quarrelsome way and is a vexatious litigant;

[96]      ORDERS Defendant Hanna
Saraffian not to, directly or indirectly, file any proceedings involving the
Plaintiff, SMBD-Jewish General Hospital before a Court of Justice or an
Administrative Tribunal in the Province of Quebec without having obtained
beforehand the written authorization of the Chief Justice of the concerned
Court or president of the Administrative Tribunal or of a judge or decider
designated by him or her;

[97]      ORDERS Defendant Hanna
Saraffian not to, directly of indirectly, file any proceedings before a Court
of Justice or an Administrative Tribunal in the Province of Quebec without
having obtained beforehand the written authorization of the Chief Justice of
the concerned Court or president of the Administrative Tribunal or of a judge
or decider designated by him or her;

[98]      ORDERS the Clerks of the
Courts and other officers of Justice of all Courts and Administrative Tribunal
of the Province of Quebec not to deliver, register in the
plumitif
or
place on the role of a Court or Administrative Tribunal of Justice in the
Province of Quebec any proceedings instituted by Defendant, Hanna Saraffian
except if prior written authorization of the Chief Justice of the concerned
Court, or president of the Administrative Tribunal or of a judge or decider
designated by him or her, appears on the proceedings;

[99]      WITH COSTS;

[100]    ORDERS provisional
execution of the part of the judgment dealing with the Motion to declare Madam
Saraffian a vexatious litigant, notwithstanding any appeal.

[
6
]

In her analysis of the Hospital's motion that
led to these conclusions, the trial judge began by referring to the text of the
relevant provisions of the
Rules of

Practice of the Superior Court in
Civil Matters
, and then considered doctrinal sources to describe what the
distinctive aspects were of quarrelsome conduct, which made reference to
examples of such conduct in Quebec and elsewhere.
[2]
Next, the trial
judge analysed the various factual elements she had observed in the course of
the trial, as reflected in Ms. Saraffian's pleadings, some exhibits which
she had authored, as well as her testimony, her manner of cross-examining
witnesses and her unflattering comments to the judge about counsel for the
Hospital and others. The trial judge also examined several of the other cases
in which Ms. Saraffian had been involved, and assessed her explanations as
to the nature of these cases. She concluded that the Court "has to balance
Madam Saraffian's right to have access to the Courts and the preservation of
judicial resources especially in these days when they are becoming scarcer and
scarcer".

[
7
]

Ms. Saraffian appealed the condemnation
against her and her mother, as well as appealing the dismissal of both
cross-demands. The Hospital did not appeal the dismissal of its claim to have
Ms. Saraffian condemned personally instead of only in a representative
capacity.

[
8
]

The Hospital then applied to dismiss the appeal
of both Mrs. Kummerman and Ms. Saraffian. On August 19 this year,
this Court (Dalphond, Hilton and Doyon, JJ.A.) granted the motion in part and dismissed
the appeal of Mrs. Kummerman on the basis that "the appeal of Martha
Kummerman was not filed by her personally or by a member of the Bar of Quebec
acting on her behalf" in that the appeal had been filed by
Ms. Saraffian, who is not a member of the Bar. The Hospital's motion to
dismiss the appeal of Ms. Saraffian, however, was dismissed inasmuch as
"at least some of the grounds of appeal of Hanna Saraffian cannot be said
to be frivolous".

[
9
]

Ms. Saraffian presented two other motions
which the same panel heard and adjudicated the same day.

[
10
]

The first of these was a motion to authorize her
to amend her inscription in appeal. The Court dismissed it given "the
irregularity of the motion to amend the inscription in appeal and the fact that
it is unnecessary for the prosecution of the appeal".

[
11
]

The second motion, dated just a few days before
the hearing, is of interest in the context of Ms. Saraffian's current
motion and bears some explanation. It is entitled "Motion requesting
permission to allow defendant Hanna Saraffian to file any necessary procedure
in court well founded in fact and in law", and is said to be made pursuant
to articles 502 and 509 of the
Code of Civil Procedure
.

[
12
]

The motion alleges, amongst other allegations
which are not relevant for present purposes, that the Superior Court judgment
is unfounded, and further asserts that Ms. Saraffian requires the freedom
to bring proceedings against the Hospital and others involved in the management
of the care of Mrs. Kummerman. The conclusions of this motion are as
follows:

A)

TO ALLOW HANNA SARAFFIAN TO PROCEED FREELY IN
FILING ANY NECESSARY PROCEDURE IN COURT AND ANY TRIBUNAL IN THE PROVINCE OF
QUEBEC UNTIL SUCH TIME THAT THE APPEAL IS HEARD AND DECIDED UPON.

B)

TO ORDER PLAINTIFF/RESPONDENT TO IMMEDIATELY REMOVE
ANY AND ALL DERROGATORY INFORMATION AND JUDGEMENT FILED AGAINST DEFENDANT HANNA
SARAFFIAN HER CREDIT RATING THAT WAS FALSELY FILED.

C)

TO ORDER TO REMOVE ANY DERROGATORY INFORMATION
FILED EVERYWERE IN THE COURTS AND THE DIFFERENT LEGAL JURISPRUDENCE SITES
POSTED ON THE INTERNET UNTIL THE APPEAL IS HEARD AND DECIDED UPON.
[3]

[
13
]

The Court rendered judgment on this motion in
the following terms:

The motion of Hanna Saraffian
requesting permission to allow her to file any necessary procedure in Court is
GRANTED

in part to the extent of allowing her to prosecute her own appeal in this case
without the prior authorization of the Chief Justice of the Quebec Court of
Appeal or the Chief Justice of any other Court in Quebec, without costs.

[
14
]

It will therefore be seen that to the extent
that Ms. Saraffian's motion sought to allow her to initiate proceedings in
the Superior Court, her application was refused.

[
15
]

Approximately six weeks later,
Ms. Saraffian then served the motion which I have before me entitled
"Motion to suspend provisional execution as per article 550 C.C.P.".
This motion relates many of the same allegations that were contained in the
motion to which I have referred in paragraphs [10], [11] and [12].

[
16
]

It asserts that the trial judge delivered
"a Despotic extremely oppressive judgment thereby completely denying
Appellant/Defendant Hanna Saraffian her Civil Rights, fundamental Rights, Human
Rights and above all her Constitutional Rights", and that she has
"not an Inherent Right and not a Contingent Right based on the Will of an
Individual of the Judiciary", but a "Constitutional Right" that
"cannot be removed by virtue of the Rules of Practice".
[4]

[
17
]

Ms. Saraffian explains in her motion that
she wishes to exercise a recourse against the Public Curator "who in
violation of the Law and the Law and Rules that govern this Office, at the
request of the Jewish General Hospital instituted several years ago a procedure
to take over Martha Kummerman, Hanna Saraffian her mother on Curatorship,
irrespective of the fact that Martha Kummerman was not, nor is she
incapacitated and thereby also Defrauding Hanna Saraffian who holds a General
Power of Attorney to act on her behalf when she so wishes", and that
"the Public Curator and the Jewish General Hospital dragged me through the
Court system for a year and a half and all in violation of the Law",
which, she says, "was designed to intimidate and to extort money from
Appellant/Defendant Hanna Saraffian".
[5]
Mrs. Saraffian
is concerned that the "deadline" within which this action must be instituted
is approaching.

[
18
]

At the hearing before me, Ms. Saraffian
also referred to her wish to bring proceedings against the Hospital arising out
of the deleterious effect of the alleged presence of asbestos within the walls
of the institution, which she says was established by a report from the
Commission
de la santé et de la sécurité du travail
upon which she intends to rely.
Indeed, she contends that the Hospital decided to bring the motion to have her
declared a vexations litigant when the subject came up during the proceedings
before the trial judge, and that the Hospital's true objective is to prevent
her from bringing a case against it related to harm caused to patients and
others, including herself, by the presence of asbestos.

[
19
]

Ms. Saraffian contends that she is being
held "Hostage in her own life"
[6]
by the prohibition
from filing legal proceedings, and that in any event, "the Courts have
other means to penalize those that abuse the system with fines and costs, Hanna
Saraffian is merely seeking Justice, and therefore a punishment against those
that wronged her that fits the crime that they committed".
[7]

She points out that the system in place does not work, inasmuch as she
attempted to contact the Chief Justice of the Superior Court on July 8 this
year, but she was "treated like a second class citizen" and "was
brushed off by the secretary with the excuse that the Chief Judge doesn't speak
to Civilians and that the only way I can communicate with the Court is in
writing". She reiterates her concern that the "prescriptive period to
take this action is not far away".

[
20
]

The conclusions of her motion read as follows:

A)

TO SUSPEND THE PROVISIONAL EXECUTION UP TO UNTIL
THE APPEAL IS HEARD AND DECIDED UPON.

B)

ORDER PLAINTIFF/RESPONDENT TO IMMEDIATELY REMOVE
ANY AND ALL LIBELIOUS AND DERROGATORY INFORMATION THAT WAS DEPOSITED AGAINST
HANNA SARAFFIAN HER CREDIT RATING FRAUDULENTLY.

C)

ORDER TO REMOVE ANY AND ALL LIBELIOUS AND
DERROGATORY INFORMATION INCLUDING THE JUDGEMENT THAT WAS FILED ON MANY
DIFFERENT WEBSITES THAT POST JURISPRUDENCE UNTIL THE APPEAL IS HEARD AND
DECIDED UPON.

D)

ORDER THE COUNSEL FOR PLAINTIFF SMBD-JEWISH
GENERAL HOSPITAL TO TO CEASE FOMENTING HATRED FO FURTHER INJURE HANNA SARAFFIAN
HER REPUTATION.
[8]

[
21
]

It will be seen that the conclusion in paragraph
A) of the motion is essentially the same as that contained in paragraph A) of
the conclusions of the motion referred to in paragraph [12], although it is
worded differently. This Court did not grant conclusion A) in the earlier
motion insofar as proceedings in the Superior Court are concerned. In addition,
it is apparent that the conclusions in paragraphs B) and C) of both motions
resemble each other.

[
22
]

Several reasons lead me to conclude that I
should not grant Ms. Saraffian's motion.

[
23
]

At the outset, it is clear that I have no
authority as a judge in chambers acting under article 550
C.C.P.
to
grant any of the conclusions in paragraphs B), C), and D) of her motion, as set
out in paragraph [20]. At most, all I can grant is Ms. Saraffian's request
that the order of provisional execution contained in paragraph [100] of the
judgment of the Superior Court be suspended.

[
24
]

Nevertheless, I am not inclined to issue such an
order.

[
25
]

First, although her request was framed in a
different way in the motion which the Court only granted in part insofar as the
prosecution of this appeal is concerned, her request to be free to institute
proceedings in any other "Court or tribunal in the province of
Quebec" was not granted. It hardly belongs to me as a judge in chambers to
effectively revise a judgment of the Court, even if it is one in which I
participated as a member of the panel.

[
26
]

Second, article 86 of the
Rules of Practice
of the Superior Court
provides a mechanism for a person who has been made
subject to an order such as the one affecting Ms. Saraffian to obtain
authorization to bring proceedings. That provision reads as follows:

86. Application for
authorization.
The application to institute or to
continue an action or application is presented to the Chief Justice or the
judge designated by the Chief Justice, and is filed in the Office of the Court
for the District of Quebec or the District of Montreal depending on the
division in which the order of prohibition was issued.  The application may be
adjudicated on the basis of the record, without a hearing.

[
27
]

In this case, Ms. Saraffian has not made an
application in the manner contemplated by that article. The fact that she may
have been told to communicate with the Chief Justice of the Superior Court in
writing, whatever the true tenor of the conversation between Ms. Saraffian
and the secretary of the Chief Justice may have been, does not mean that she is
unable to prepare and present the necessary motion. I am therefore not
satisfied that Ms. Saraffian has demonstrated that the system currently in
place is ineffective to the point that I should suspend the order issued by the
trial judge.

[
28
]

As far as the deadline for any action she may
wish to take being prescribed, it is impossible to judge the seriousness of
this contention without knowing more about such actions and when precisely the
respective prescriptive periods began to run. Her motion lacks adequate detail
in this respect, and does not attach a copy of the actions she proposes to
institute.

[
29
]

Finally, the case-law is constant that in order
to succeed in a motion to suspend provisional execution that has been ordered
by a trial judgment, an applicant must show that the order of provisional
execution is the result of the flawed exercise of the judge's discretion, and
that since the judgment benefits from a presumption of validity, the applicant
has the burden to demonstrate its apparent weakness.
[9]
While I do not
presume to judge the outcome of the appeal on the merits, I believe my summary
of the judge's process of reasoning in paragraph [6] demonstrates that the
judgment of the Superior Court suffers from no such apparent weakness.

[
30
]

I therefore dismiss Ms. Saraffian's motion,
with costs.

ALLAN R. HILTON, J.A.

Hanna Saraffian

In person

Mtre Caroline Matte

BORDEN LADNER GERVAIS

For the respondent

Date of hearing:

November 10, 2004

[1]
Article
84 of the
Rules of Practice of the Superior Court in Civil Matters

provides as follows: "If a person acts in a quarrelsome manner, that is,
if that person exercises litigious rights in an excessive or unreasonable
manner, the Court may prohibit that person from instituting an action or an
application without having first obtained prior judicial authorization."

[2]
